shared_context.topic: stopping Prozac due to side effects

atoms.1: If the side effects of Prozac (fluoxetine) become too much, it is generally recommended to wean down the medication rather than stopping it abruptly.
atoms.2: Prozac is also known as fluoxetine.
atoms.3: Abrupt discontinuation of Prozac can lead to withdrawal symptoms.
atoms.4: Withdrawal symptoms from abrupt discontinuation of Prozac may include dizziness.
atoms.5: Withdrawal symptoms from abrupt discontinuation of Prozac may include headache.
atoms.6: Withdrawal symptoms from abrupt discontinuation of Prozac may include nausea.
atoms.7: Withdrawal symptoms from abrupt discontinuation of Prozac may include irritability.
atoms.8: The weaning process typically involves gradually reducing the dose over a period of time.
atoms.9: The weaning process should be done under the guidance of a healthcare provider.
atoms.10: The specific tapering schedule can vary depending on the individual’s current dose.
atoms.11: The specific tapering schedule can vary depending on the individual’s duration of use.
atoms.12: The specific tapering schedule can vary depending on the individual’s response to the medication.

snippets.output: If the side effects of Prozac (fluoxetine) become too much, it is generally recommended to wean down the medication rather than stopping it abruptly.
Abrupt discontinuation of Prozac can lead to withdrawal symptoms, which may include dizziness, headache, nausea, and irritability.
The weaning process typically involves gradually reducing the dose over a period of time and should be done under the guidance of a healthcare provider.
The specific tapering schedule can vary depending on the individual’s current dose, duration of use, and response to the medication.
